  C. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council Regular
  Meeting of February 5, 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  D. STATE OF HOMELAND SECURITY GRANT PROGRAM (SHSGP) FOR FIRE
  DEPARTMENT RADIOS

  The San Gabriel Fire Department (SGFD) was awarded funds from the 2017
  State Homeland Security Grant Program in the amount of $17,000. SGFD is able
  to use these funds to fund projects from the Department of Homeland Security
  Approved Equipment List (AEL) and to provide training. SGFD is allocated
  $17,000 of which $15,000 is dedicated to equipment and $2,000 is dedicated
  toward mobilization exercises. The funds would be used to purchase the
  equipment related to portable generators and will be used to provide backfill
  for members attending mobilization exercises if they are on-duty.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Increase the estimated revenue budget by $17,000 to Revenue Account
  186-3215; and
  2. Increase the Fire Department Budget by $17,000 to Account No. 122-761-
  57-99-380; and
  3. Authorize the Fire Chief to accept the San Gabriel Homeland Security
  Program grant and purchase the items under the City’s purchasing policy.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 19, 2019  3
   E. AMENDED TOLLING AGREEMENT

  In January 2019, the City approved an extension of a tolling agreement between
  the Firefighters’ Association and its members and the City that permits them to
  preserve the affected firefighter employee’s wage-and-hour claims while the
  parties work toward a resolution of their dispute with the City without the costs
  of a lawsuit. However, subsequent to the Council’s approval, the Firefighters’
  Association requested certain minor modifications to the approved agreement.
  As these changes are not adverse to the City, they have now been presented
  for Council’s approval.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the amended “new tolling
  agreement” between the City of San Gabriel and the San Gabriel Firefighters’
  Association.

  F. METRO / CALIFORNIA CONGESTION MANAGEMENT PROGRAM (CMP) –
  OPT OUT RESOLUTION NO. 19-05

  Metro is required by state law to prepare and update on a biennial basis the
  Congestion Management Program (CMP) for the County of Los Angeles. The
  CMP Process was established as part of a 1990 legislative package to implement
  Proposition 111, which increased the state gas tax from 9 cents to 18 cents. The
  intent of the CMP was to tie the appropriation of new gas tax revenues to
  congestion reduction efforts by improving land use / transportation
  coordination. While the CMP requirement was one of the pioneering efforts to
  conduct performance-based planning, the approach has become antiquated
  and expensive.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-05 electing to
  be exempt from the Congestion Management Program (CMP) in accordance
  with the CMP State statute.

  G. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH JMDIAZ, INCORPORATED
  FOR DESIGN & ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR INTERSECTION SAFETY
  IMPROVEMENT PROJECT AT LAS TUNAS DRIVE / MISSION DRIVE, LAS
  TUNAS DRIVE / DEL MAR AVENUE, LAS TUNAS DRIVE / COUNTRY CLUB
  DRIVE AND SAN GABRIEL BOULEVARD / LIVE OAK STREET

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 19, 2019  4
   The City is proposing a project to improve traffic and pedestrian safety along
  the Las Tunas Drive and the San Gabriel Boulevard corridors at four
  intersections. The proposed project consists of the installation of protected left
  turn phases for the eastbound / westbound at the intersection of Las Tunas
  Drive / Mission Drive; the installation of protected left turn phases for the
  northbound / southbound at the intersection of Las Tunas Drive / Del Mar
  Avenue; and the installation of crosswalk visibility enhancement and the
  rectangular rapid flashing beacons (RRFBs) for the uncontrolled crosswalks at
  the intersection of San Gabriel Boulevard / Live Oak Street. Funds for these
  Professional Services are available in Account No. 122-800-57-97-103.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve a professional services
  agreement with JMDiaz, Inc. in the amount not to exceed $47,410 (including a
  10% contingency in the amount of $4,310) for professional design and
  engineering services for Intersection Safety Improvement Project at Las Tunas
  Drive / Mission Drive, Las Tunas Drive / Del Mar Avenue, Las Tunas Drive /
  Country Club Drive, and San Gabriel Boulevard / Live Oak Street.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 19-03, APPROVING EMPLOYMENT
  AGREEMENT BETWEEN PAULA CHAMBERLAIN AND THE CITY OF SAN
  GABRIEL FOR INTERIM FINANCE DIRECTOR

  Finance Director Tom Marston has announced his retirement from the City of
  San Gabriel, to be effective February 28, 2019. While Human Resources
  conducts a recruitment to fill the position, staff recommends appointing retired
  annuitant Paula Chamberlain as Interim Finance Director. If Council approves
  Resolution No. 19-03, Ms. Chamberlain will start on March 4, 2019.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-03, approving
  an employment agreement between Paula Chamberlain and the City of San
  Gabriel for Interim Finance Director.

3.  PUBLIC COMMENT

  Camelia Vera expressed her concerns regarding illegal signs posted on city streets and
  street scarring on the edge of San Marino Avenue between Leslie Drive and Roses
  Road and Roses Road and Longden Drive.

  City Manager Lazzaretto responded that he will look into the reason why concerns
  submitted online have not been addressed, and explained that the conditions on San
  Marino Avenue are due to the recent replacement of the waterline in preparation of

  the scheduled paving project that will be underway once the weather permits.

  Sandra Armenta Lopez, representative from the Office of Senator Susan Rubio, invited

  the City Council and community to Coffee and Conversation with Senator Susan Rubio
  scheduled to take place on Saturday, February 20, 2019, beginning at 9: 30 a. m., at the
  Arcadia Public Library Auditorium at 20 W. Duarte Road, Arcadia.

  City Manager Lazzaretto offered to make the invitation available on the City' s website.

4.  CONSENT  CALENDAR

  Program ( CMP) — Opt Out Resolution No. 19- 05 out of order for discussion.

  City Attorney Lemieux requested that Consent Calendar Item 4C Minutes of the
  Regular meeting be approved as amended to clarify that the 50% figure refers to the
  Sales, Marketing, and Communication allocation; and announced a correction on the

  Agenda regarding Item 4D removing " for Fire Department Radios" from the title.

  F.  METRO /  CALIFORNIA  CONGESTION  MANAGEMENT  PROGRAM ( CMP) — OPT

  OUT RESOLUTION  NO. 19- 05

  City Council adopted Resolution No.  19- 05,  electing to be exempt from the
  Congestion  Management  Program ( CMP)  in  accordance  with  the  CMP  State

  statute.

  In response to questions from Vice Mayor Pu and Council  Member Menchaca,
  Principal Engineer Algis Marciuska explained that there are no disadvantages to

  electing to be exempt from the program because the program' s measurements
  have become outdated and the City would not lose any funds by electing out of
  the program; and that a majority of the cities within the County must elect to be

  exempt from the program. Metro is still in the process of colleting  the required
  amount of cities to reach the majority; and a few cities have elected to be exempt
  from the plan with a few others still in the process of bringing the item forward for
  their Council' s consideration.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Pu, seconded by Council Member Menchaca, to
  approve Consent Calendar Items 4A — 4B and 4D — 4G as presented,  and  4C as

  amended.

8.  CITY MANAGER' S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto requested volunteers for the KaBOOM! Playground Build Day
  scheduled on March 14, 2019, commented on the Los Angeles Clippers attending in
  support of the event, and invited those interested to contact the Community Services
  Department for more information. He thanked the Fire Department for the experience

  and knowledge he gained while attending the City' s Community Emergency Response
  Team ( CERT)  Program and encouraged the City Council and members  of the

  community to take part in CERT.

9.  CITY COUNCIL BUSINESS/ COMMITTEE  REPORTS

  Council Member Costanzo reported on a meeting she attended at the Los Angeles
  County Sanitation District and announced a hazardous and a -waste event scheduled
  to take place on Saturday, March 9, 2019 at the Mission Playhouse Parking Lot, with
  more information available on the Los Angeles County Sanitation District' s website.
  She expressed her gratitude to staff for their efforts in planning and organizing
  another successful Lunar New Year Festival and asked that the dance competition be
  brought back to the festival.

  Council Member Liao spoke about the ceremonial event held on Tuesday, February
  12, 2019 in the Council Chambers at which a carved a stone statue of Toypurina,

  heroine of the Gabrielino- Tongva people, was dedicated to the City, and thanked City
  Manager  Lazzaretto  for attending  the  event.  He  stated  that  members  of  the

  community interested in learning more about the statue of Toypurina should contact
  Julie Sorensen,  Los Angeles County Librarian, and expressed his appreciation for the
  rich history the City has. He reported on a meeting he attended with San Gabriel Valley
  Civic Alliance where he learned about a group interested in forming a Joint Power
  Financing Authority with a few cities to fund bonds for projects in the participating
  cities. In closing, he commented on various measures and propositions that assist with
  funding storm water projects.

  Council Member Menchaca thanked Vice Mayor Pu and City staff for their work in
  preparation of the Lunar New Year Festival and commented on her experiences

  volunteering at various non- profit booths. She announced that 211 LA County will be
  hosting a Disaster Preparedness Big and Small Fair at the Mission Playhouse on
  Saturday, February 23, 2019. She mentioned that she will be joining the City Manager

   at a Ballot Measure Training Academy that will be held by the League of California
  Cities in Monterey Park and spoke about the importance of understanding the issues
  the City needs to be aware of.

  Vice  Mayor  Pu  expressed  his interest in attending  the  Ballot  Measure  Training
  Academy and requested that the information be forwarded to him.  He spoke  about

  the future of elections and the movement towards Vote Centers instead of multiple

  polling stations, expressed his concerns that there had been no Vote Centers accepted
  south of Mission Road, and stated that he will follow up with the County to make sure
  the City will have Vote Centers that will adequately serve the entire population. He
  expressed his gratitude to the City Council and to staff for the teamwork it took to
  create a successful Lunar Festival and stated that he will work hard to bring back the
  dance  competition.  He  mentioned  that  he  will  be  attending  the  Council  of

  Governments  Transportation
  meeting scheduled for Thursday, February 21, 2019
  where he is expected to be elected as Vice Chair of the committee with hopes of

  serving the region well.

  Mayor Harrington expressed his gratitude to staff and recognized the amount of

  planning necessary to produce a successful festival like Lunar New Year Festival, and
  expressed his desire to bring the dance competition back to the festival. He announced
  the San Gabriel  Education  Foundation " Toast to the Future"  Fundraiser  scheduled  to

  take place on Thursday, February 21, 2019 at Ogopogo Brewing, and noted  that the

  tickets have sold out.

  Council Member Liao stated that he had tickets available and would like to invite the
  public to attend San Gabriel Civic Alliance Sector Awards scheduled to take place on

  Friday, March 29, 2019 located at the Double Tree Hotel in Baldwin Park.

10. CLOSED SESSION — None.
